h: Rolling Stones, Roman Villas and Green Valleys
p: Music fans, here's one for you. Dartford is where Mick Jagger and Keith Richards famously bumped into each other on a railway platform in 1961, a chance meeting that led to the birth of the Rolling Stones. The town is proud of the connection, and the Mick Jagger Centre is a local arts venue named after the singer.

Back to the bouncing for a moment. Save time by filling in waivers before you arrive, keep your grip socks for next time and bring a drink for after the session. Ask the team about quieter sessions if you've got very young children, as busy weekend slots can be a bit of a whirlwind for toddlers.

A trip to the Darent Valley south of town is a lovely contrast to the noise of the trampoline park. Lullingstone Roman Villa at Eynsford, run by English Heritage, has some remarkable mosaics and tells the story of the people who lived there centuries ago. Nearby Lullingstone Castle has a World Garden full of plants from across the globe, and the countryside around Shoreham and Eynsford is great for gentle walks along the river.

Closer to town, Dartford Heath is a big open space for a breath of fresh air, and the Thames riverside is just to the north. With Bluewater on one side and the Kent countryside on the other, Dartford is a good base for mixing indoor fun with a slice of the outdoors.
